message.content:
**Proteins commonly found in the mammalian plasma membrane** | Category | Typical Functions | Representative Examples | |----------|-------------------|-------------------------| | **Integral (Trans‑membrane) Proteins** | Span the lipid bilayer; form pores/channels or serve as carriers. | • Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase
• Glucose transporter GLUT1 / GLUT4
• Aquaporin‑1
• Voltage‑gated K⁺ channel Kv11.1
• Connexin hemichannels (gap junctions)
• Receptor tyrosine kinases (EGFR, HER2) – often single‑pass transmembrane domains | | **Peripheral Membrane Proteins** | Associate loosely via electrostatic interactions or through covalent attachment to lipids or other proteins. | • GPI‑anchored proteins (e.g., Thyroglobulin, Prion protein)
• Cytoplasmic tail‑binding proteins (e.g., β‑catenin binding to E‑cadherin)
• Signal transduction adaptors (e.g., Grb2, SHP‑2) | | **Cell Adhesion Molecules** | Mediate homophilic/heterophilic contacts between cells or with extracellular matrix. | • Cadherins (E‑cadherin, N‑cadherin)
• Integrins (α5β1, αvβ3)
• Selectins (L-, P-, E-selectin) | | **Immune Recognition & Signaling Receptors** | Detect antigens, cytokines, or pathogen‐associated patterns. | • T‑cell receptor complex (CD3ζ, TCRαβ)
• B‑cell receptor (IgM/IgD heavy/light chains)
• Major histocompatibility complex class I/II (HLA-A/B/C, HLA-DRA/DQA…)
• Pattern recognition receptors (TLR4, NOD‑like receptors) | | **Enzymes Anchored to the Surface** | Catalyze reactions directly at the membrane interface. | • Alkaline phosphatase (ecto‑enzyme)
• Phosphatidylinositol phosphate kinase (PI3K catalytic subunit p110α)
• Matrix metalloproteinases (MT1-MMP) | | **Transporter & Carrier Families** | Move ions, metabolites, or small molecules across the membrane. | • Sodium–glutamate cotransporter SLC1A5
• Chloride intracellular channel CLIC1
• Nicotinamide nucleotide transhydrogenase (mitochondrial inner membrane, not plasma) | ### How they’re organized * **Single‑pass (monotopic)**: One hydrophobic segment crosses once (e.g., hormone receptors). * **Multi‑pass (polytopic)**: Multiple segments create pore structures (e.g., ion channels). * **Anchoring mechanisms**: * **Hydrophobic core insertion** (integral). * **Post‑translational modifications** (palmitoylation, myristoylation, glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchors). --- #### Quick Takeaway The plasma membrane hosts thousands of distinct proteins—each tailored to its role: | Role | Protein Type | Example | |------|--------------|--------| | Ion movement | Transmembrane channel | Voltage‑gated Ca²⁺ channel Cav1.2 | | Nutrient uptake | Transporter | Glucose transporter GLUT4 | | Cell communication | GPCR | Dopamine D₂ receptor | | Immune surveillance | MHC molecule | HLA‑DR | | Structural integrity | Cadherin | E‑cadherin | | Signal amplification | Enzyme | Src family tyrosine kinase Fyn | These proteins together maintain cellular homeostasis, mediate signal transduction, enable nutrient exchange, and facilitate intercellular interaction—all essential for life’s processes.
